newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SML profits up, says worst over for salvage.
newsitem.headline: SML profits up, says worst over for salvage.

text.p: Sembawang Maritime Ltd (SML), which reported better than expected 1996 earnings on Tuesday, will rationalise its shrinking salvage business further through alliances, president Billy Lee said.
Lee said SML, which is engaged in salvage, marine transportation, port operations, shiprepair and ship-related services, will maintain its core salvage business although it was a "sunset industry".
In its heyday in the late 1980s, salvage contributed about 80 percent of the group's earnings.

The group was also expecting higher contribution from its regional port and shipping businesses. It also plans to increase its stake in Hong Kong Wah Kwong Shipping to about 20 percent from 12.3 percent at the end of 1996.
Analysts said they would recommend a buy on SML given its improved earnings but added they were wary about its growth prospects.

"I would maintain a buy recommendation because its results were above expectations. But I don't feel comfortable that some of its profits are generated by vessel sales," said one analyst with a local institution.
In 1996, SML reaped an estimated pre-tax profit of S$10 million from its sale of two older barges and one tug from SEMCO, the company said in a statement accompanying its results.
SML shares ended S$0.02 down at S$3.78 on a turnover of 46,000 shares.
